name: NanoHUB
description: NanoHUB adapts and unifies NanoMDM, NanoCMD, and KMFDDM into a single Apple MDM server binary, exposing MDM check-in/command endpoints plus their combined REST APIs (push, workflows, DDM declarations) behind one HTTP listener. This installs the reference nanohub server with file-based storage, generating a random API key for HTTP Basic Auth on the API endpoints.

notes.text: This gets the reference NanoHUB server running with file-based storage and a random API key. It does not configure an MDM CA certificate, APNs push certificate, or ABM/ASM/DEP tokens - those are required before real devices can enroll. Edit /opt/nanohub_data/nanohub.env (adds flags via systemd Environment/EnvironmentFile) and see the Operations Guide for -ca, -intermediate, and push configuration, then run 'systemctl restart nanohub'.

For the CA certificate needed by -ca / NANOHUB_CA, install the companion SCEP script (json/scep.json, micromdm/scep) - it generates a CA and issues the device identity certificates NanoHUB authenticates enrollments against.
The API endpoints (/api/v1/nanomdm/, /api/v1/nanocmd/, /api/v1/ddm/) use HTTP Basic Auth with username 'nanohub' and the generated API key as the password.

File storage keeps all enrollment/command state under /opt/nanohub_data/db. For multi-node deployments, NanoHUB also supports a MySQL 8.0.19+ backend, but it requires manually creating the NanoMDM, NanoCMD, and KMFDDM schemas yourself - not set up by this script.
